item.title: Sebi to issue AI usage guidelines for capital markets, focus on investor protection
item.description: The Sebi chief said the proposed guidelines would focus on establishing appropriate guardrails for AI use, including disclosures, accountability of regulated entities, and a 'human-in-the-loop' approach.
item.content:encoded:
Markets regulator Sebi will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the capital markets, its chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said, emphasising the need to balance technological innovation with investor protection.

The Sebi chief said the proposed guidelines would focus on establishing appropriate guardrails for AI use, including disclosures, accountability of regulated entities and a 'human-in-the-loop' approach to ensure that critical decisions are subject to human oversight.

In June 2025, Sebi (Securities and Exchange Board of India) floated a consultation paper proposing guiding principles for responsible usage of artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) applications/models in securities markets.

These guiding principles are intended to optimise benefits and minimise potential risks associated with the integration of AI/ML based applications in securities markets to safeguard investor protection, market integrity, and financial stability.

Speaking at the inauguration of Sebi's pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, on Saturday, Pandey said the regulator has been continuously strengthening its cybersecurity framework to address rising cyber threats.

He highlighted growing concerns over cyberattacks targeting financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms, as well as digital frauds involving social media influencers.

Following emerging threats, the regulator also introduced a structured incident response mechanism in May this year, aligned with the Financial Stability Board's FIRE reporting template, he said at the sidelines of an event here on Saturday.

On quantum computing-related risks, the Chairman said Sebi is undertaking an inventory of cryptographic systems and identifying areas where cryptography is being used to assess potential vulnerabilities.

He said markets globally are preparing for the risks posed by quantum computing, with concerns expected to become more pronounced around 2032-35, and stressed the need to complete preparations well in advance.

On AI adoption, he said Sebi has also developed several supervisory tools, including its 'Sudarshan' tool, which is being demonstrated at international regulatory forums.

The regulator is also working on strengthening its AI capabilities through international initiatives and supervisory toolkits, he added.

The Chairman further said Sebi is reviewing the regulatory framework to ensure that the use of AI by market participants does not compromise investor protection, market safety or integrity.

On startups and the listing framework, the Sebi chief also said the regulator has formed a working group to examine ways to make the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) more attractive for startups, particularly deep-tech and biotech companies that require long gestation periods before generating profits.

He said the existing platform has not gained the desired traction, and the regulator is reviewing potential changes to help such companies access public markets at an earlier stage.

The objective is to provide investors clarity about the higher risks associated with such businesses while allowing them to participate in their long-term growth potential.

However, he declined to share details of budget-related discussions.

item.title: Razorpay, Sembcorp Green Infra get Sebi nod to float IPOs
item.description: Razorpay filed draft documents with Sebi via the confidential route in June for an IPO.
item.content:encoded:
Fintech firm Razorpay Software Ltd and Sembcorp Green Infra, a renewable energy independent power producer, have secured Sebi's approval to launch initial public offerings (IPO), an update with the markets regulator showed on Friday.

Razorpay filed draft documents with Sebi via the confidential route in June for an IPO.

Sembcorp Green Infra filed preliminary papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) in August to raise up to Rs 3,750 crore through an IPO.

After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations to Razorpay and Sembcorp Green Infra on November 3 and November 13, respectively, the update showed.

Sebi's observations mark an important step in the IPO process, allowing the companies to proceed with preparations for their public issues, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.

Razorpay did not disclose the size of the proposed issue. However, people familiar with the matter estimate the issue size in the range of Rs 5,000-6,000 crore.

Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay offers payment acceptance, banking, payouts, payroll, lending and other financial services through an integrated platform. The company serves millions of businesses across India, ranging from startups and small and medium enterprises to large corporates.

Razorpay attained unicorn status in 2020 and has since expanded beyond payments into a broader financial services ecosystem for businesses. Its offerings enable merchants to manage collections, payouts, payroll, cash flows and access to capital through a single platform.

The company is backed by investors like Peak XV Partners, GIC, Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Lone Pine Capital, Alkeon Capital and TCV.

The confidential filing route allows companies to submit draft offer documents to Sebi for review without immediately disclosing sensitive business information to the public.

According to the draft red herring prospectus, Sembcorp Green Infra's proposed IPO is entirely a fresh issue of equity shares with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component.

The IPO proceeds will be used for payment of certain borrowings by the company and the subsidiaries.

The proposed capital raise will help strengthen its balance sheet as it scales up its renewable energy portfolio.

Sembcorp Green Infra had 3.60 GW of operational renewable energy capacity and about 4.04 GW/GWh under construction as of March 31, 2026. Its under-construction portfolio includes 2.61 GW of renewable energy capacity and 1,433 MWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity.

The company is also increasing its focus on complex renewable projects, including hybrid, storage-backed, round-the-clock (RTC) and firm and dispatchable renewable energy (FDRE) projects.

Promoted by Sembcorp Utilities Pte Ltd and Sembcorp Industries Ltd, SGIL has 105 projects across 13 states and union territories.

Earlier this month, Nasdaq-listed travel booking platform MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary received Sebi's approval to launch its maiden public offering.

item.title: One outage, millions affected. What went wrong at Microsoft?
item.description: Problems with Exchange Online spread across Microsoft 365 and external businesses, highlighting how dependent workplaces have become on shared cloud infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
Outlook marks the official start of the working day for millions globally. It also serves as a hub for daily workplace communication and scheduling across the world.

So, when Microsoft’s email service began failing on Thursday, November 12, the disruption quickly spread beyond missed messages to calendars, workplace tools, and businesses that depend on its cloud systems.

The massive outage continued into Friday, November 13, showing how a fault in one widely used service can cause ripples across the entire work ecosystem.

What happened and when

Microsoft’s incident records list Exchange Online incident EX1550543 as starting at 4.17 pm UTC on Thursday, or 9.47 pm in India. Users were unable to connect to their Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods.

Microsoft Exchange Online is the back-end server that stores and manages user data, while Microsoft Outlook is the front-end app used to view and interact with the data.

The wider Microsoft 365 incident, MO1550821, which disrupted multiple Microsoft 365 enterprise and consumer services worldwide, began at 6.26 pm UTC, or 11.56 pm IST.

First reports came from the Americas, but Microsoft later warned that users in any region could be affected.

Downdetector, a real-time platform that tracks online service disruptions and outages, recorded more than 1,30,000 reports of Outlook problems in the United States at its peak on Thursday afternoon. In India, complaints began shortly before midnight and reached 2,157 at 11.42 pm. Reports rose again to 1,960 at 8.42 am on Friday as people started work.

In its latest post on X, Microsoft said traffic-optimisation measures were producing positive results for service stability and capacity. It was applying these measures more widely across affected regions as it worked towards sustained recovery. While this indicates progress, it is not an all-clear from the company.

Microsoft directed users to incident MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin centre or its public status page. MO1550821 is one of the official incident tracking IDs assigned by Microsoft for the ongoing service degradation and outage. 

Why this happened

Microsoft’s explanation emerged in stages. It first said a number of servers had unexpectedly become unavailable, putting extra load on the remaining infrastructure. The higher load, it stressed, was not caused by a sudden rise in customer traffic.

Later, Microsoft said a process on affected servers responsible for establishing secure connections had become overwhelmed, causing servers to stop handling requests. It also began rolling back a recent network configuration change that it said correlated with the start of the incident. Earlier updates had said no recent change had been linked to the problem.

Recovery was complicated with servers becoming unresponsive again when traffic returned. Microsoft tried restarting and rebuilding affected servers, restricting certain types of traffic, moving connections to alternative routes, and improving capacity. The challenge was not to simply bring servers back online, but also to keep them stable as traffic returned.

Microsoft said it had no indication that malicious activity had caused the outage. The precise root cause remained unconfirmed, and the company said it would publish a post-incident report.

Why so many services were affected

Exchange Online is Microsoft’s cloud-hosted email and calendar service. Other Microsoft 365 features use it for mail, contacts, calendar entries, and meeting information. When Exchange Online became unreliable, features that depended on it were disrupted even where the wider app was still running.

Users struggled to access mailboxes through Outlook on the web, desktop, and other connection methods, while email delivery was delayed. Copilot for Microsoft 365 failed to load or respond, or struggled to retrieve work data. In Teams, calendars and meeting scheduling were affected, but core calls, meetings, group chats and channel messages remained available. SharePoint files stored directly in the service remained accessible, although some connected features were affected.

Microsoft also listed problems with specific functions in Planner, To Do, Defender, Purview, Power BI, Intune, and Microsoft Graph, a set of programming interfaces that lets software exchange data with Microsoft services.

The impact beyond Microsoft, including India

Reuters reported that OpenAI and Anthropic had problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors, which link the AI services to users’ work information.

In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air said their email-support services were affected. There was no indication that flights were disrupted.

The effects reached public institutions too. Reuters reported that Australian government bodies, including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation and the Australian Federal Police; Japan’s government IT infrastructure; and users in the US House of Representatives were affected. Taiwanese financial firms also reported disruption to fund-management work.

Social media saw a meme fest. On X, users combined frustration with humour, as they joked about closing laptops, skipping meetings, and taking Friday off. Others linked another Microsoft outage to the long wait for Grand Theft Auto VI.

Different incidents, similar risks

This is not Microsoft’s first major 365 disruption this year. Another outage began on August 31 and was resolved on September 3. Microsoft attributed it to a problem with a core authentication configuration used by several services, affecting Exchange Online and parts of Copilot, OneDrive and SharePoint. However, that was a different, identified problem.

A cloud-related outage similar to the current disruption happened in October at Google, when an electrical failure at a data-centre facility disrupted services in Google Cloud’s europe-west2 region, a cloud computing data centre location in London.

Google’s incident report said the main impact lasted about six hours and eight minutes. The cause was different, but the incident showed how a local infrastructure failure can affect customers across a cloud region.

The CrowdStrike incident in July 2024 was different again. A faulty software update from the cybersecurity firm caused Windows machines worldwide to crash. Microsoft estimated that 8.5 million devices were affected. The mechanism was different, but the disruption underlined the risks when a small number of providers underpin critical systems.

What happens next

The test now is whether the traffic-optimisation changes keep servers stable as Microsoft increases traffic and capacity across regions. The company has promised a post-incident report covering the root cause and measures to prevent a repeat.

Customers need to know not only what failed but also why safeguards did not contain the disruption sooner.

The ongoing incident shows how dependent workplaces have become on shared cloud infrastructure.

For organisations, the lesson is to plan for a key provider failing. They must keep emergency contact channels outside the main email system, make critical information available by other means, and maintain alternative ways to reach staff and customers. Cloud services make apps work together, but these connections can also create shared points of failure. Products may look separate but they rely on the same underlying systems.

Edited by Swetha Kannan

item.title: India, US have agreed on preferential market access for Indian goods in America: Piyush Goyal
item.description: India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement in February.
item.content:encoded:
India and the US have already agreed that Indian goods in the American market will receive preferential market access compared to competitor nations, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday.

India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement in February.

The deal was to be signed earlier, but changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.

"This was already agreed between the leaders - President (Donald) Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi when they announced that we have both come to a broad framework agreement a few months ago and it has been acknowledged that India will get preferential trade access in the US with lower duties than our competitor countries," Goyal told reporters in Cairo.

He is here on a two-day visit to discuss ways to boost trade and investment between India and Egypt.

The minister was replying to a question about the US assurance that Indian goods will get preferential market access.

An official has recently stated that the US has assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over competing countries under the proposed bilateral trade agreement (BTA), with both sides working to conclude the first tranche by the end of the current financial year.

"We will have to see how the tariff framework unfolds. We are working towards closing the first tranche by the end of this financial year. Talks are going for the first tranche and the broader BTA," the official said last week.

The extent of the advantage to Indian goods, however, will depend on the tariff framework eventually agreed upon.

After the US Supreme Court struck down the Trump's reciprocal tariffs that were the basis of negotiations, the US is using alternate mechanisms to put up a new tariff architecture in place using provisions of the Trade Act.

item.title: Paytm gets RBI's in-principle nod to revive wallet business through new subsidiary
item.description: Paytm’s subsidiary PPSL has received the RBI’s in-principle approval to issue prepaid instruments such as wallets, but it must submit a system audit report within six months.
item.content:encoded:
Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, has received the Reserve Bank of India's in-principle authorisation to set up and operate a payment system for issuing prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), the category that covers digital wallets. The company informed the exchanges in a regulatory filing on Friday.

The RBI's Department of Payment and Settlement Systems granted the approval under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, in a letter dated 13 November. It responds to an application PPSL made on 31 December 2025. The approval is subject to compliance with the RBI's Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments of 27 August 2021, as updated from time to time.

The nod is only a first step. PPSL can begin issuing prepaid instruments only after it receives final authorisation, or a Certificate of Authorisation. To get there, it must commission a system audit, including a cybersecurity audit, from a CERT-In empanelled auditor or a qualified information systems auditor. 

The audit must follow the RBI's Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank payment system operators, dated 5 November 2026. The report must reach the RBI within six months, failing which the in-principle approval lapses automatically and final authorisation will not be considered. The RBI also reminded PPSL that any change in its shareholding or ownership would require prior approval under its 4 July 2022 norms for non-bank payment system operators.

One 97 said it had flagged the wallet licence application in its Q1 FY2027 earnings release.

The wallet business was earlier run through Paytm Payments Bank, and after regulatory restrictions in 2024, customers were barred from adding money to their wallets, though existing balances could be withdrawn. The RBI cancelled the bank's licence on 24 April 2026, citing non-compliance with licensing conditions. Paytm has said a wallet would add to the completeness of its consumer payments offerings.

On the bourses, Paytm's stock was affected by the announcement. The shares traded at Rs 1,931.30 on the NSE at 3.06 pm, up 0.33% from the previous close of Rs 1,925. They had dipped to Rs 1,906.70 around midday. The bulk of the recent gain came a day earlier: the stock closed at a fresh 52-week high of Rs 1,925 on 12 November after a 7.31% jump, and has nearly doubled from its 52-week low of Rs 930.60 on 30 March 2026. It still trades below the Rs 2,150 IPO issue price.

item.title: (Weekly funding roundup Nov 7-14) VC inflow drops to its lowest level in 2026
item.description: The second week of November saw venture capital funding into Indian startups drop to its lowest level for the year till now due to weak deal activity.
item.content:encoded:
Weekly venture capital funding into Indian startups has dipped to the lowest level for the year till now due to a combination of the festive period and a lower number of deals.

The total venture capital funding for the second week of November was just $26 million from 11 deals. In comparison, the previous week saw a total amount of $263 million.

This is the lowest ever VC funding raised by Indian startups on a weekly basis for 2026. Prior to this, the lowest level was in the last week of May when the amount was $66 million.

This development reveals the challenges the Indian startup ecosystem continues to face in raising capital, amid the volatile macro economic environment.

The Indian startup ecosystem still greatly relies on overseas money. The increased trade tension among countries has curbed the flow of capital. However, the bigger challenge is the absence of a credible AI story in the country.

In the major VC ecosystems across the globe, it is the AI segment that has cornered the highest share of capital. This is particularly evident in the US where AI startups have raised a considerable amount of money.

In contrast, India has just a handful number of credible AI startups. This has been one of the key factors for the lower VC funding this year in the startup ecosystem.

The total VC funding for 2026 is unlikely to cross the level of 2025 given the current trends. In 2025, the Indian startup ecosystem raised $12.1 billion. The first ten months of 2026 saw VC funding of $10.4 billion, and the last two months may not see any significant VC activity.

item.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 13, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Friday, November 13, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
From Jensen Huang’s latest affair report to Sachin Tendulkar joining Recykal as a strategic investor, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.

Latest News

The race to find Nvidia's next chief begins

Nvidia has begun its search for a permanent chief executive officer after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned on November 12, ending a 33-year run at the held. The company board has said it would consider candidates from inside and outside the company.

Meanwhile, the chief financial officer Colette Kress has been appointed the interim CEO.On November 12, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang also had an intimate relationship with another female Nvidia employee, whose identity it did not disclose. 

Read More

Fusion CX forays into German market with its latest acquisition

Fusion CX will be acquiring 100% of German call-centre / BPO group Impacx. The company has signed the binding agreement with impacx effective November 1, 2026, and the acquisition is subject to regulatory and statutory approvals. The acquisition marks Fusion CX’s first foray into the German market.

Impacx, which has run AI in live client operations since 2018, recorded about €11.9 million (about $13.2 million) in revenue in 2025 and has around 250 employees, with nearshore partners in Croatia and Greece extending its delivery.

Funding News

Sachin Tendulkar joins Recykal as a strategic investor

Sachin Tendulkar has joined Recykal as a strategic investor, after the startup raised a bridge round of $23 million.

The association aim to inspire a nationwide shift in how Indians think about waste, encouraging every citizen to see it not as something to discard, but as a valuable resource that can be recovered, returned and given a second life.

As the strategic investor, Tendulkar will help champion a nationwide movement to make responsible waste behaviour an everyday habit, carrying forward the spirit of Swachh Bharat into its next chapter.

Other News

Varaha’s community-led biochar project achieves a BeZero Carbon ex ante Rating of A.pre

Varaha announced that its community-led biochar project, Agnisparsh has been assigned a BeZero Carbon ex ante Rating of A.pre, with low project execution risk, as of October 2026.

Set up in Western India, the project at full operation, will run approximately 450 Kon-Tiki kilns across multiple mobile sites, turning biomass from local smallholder farms into biochar. Biomass in the region is commonly burned in the field after harvest. The project instead converts them into biochar, most of which goes back, free of charge, to the smallholder farmers who supplied the biomass.

(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

item.title: Microsoft’s global outage; Vidya Balan’s call to put child safety first
item.description: Problems with Exchange Online spread across Microsoft 365 and external businesses, highlighting how dependent workplaces have become on shared cloud infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader,

The race to find Jensen Huang’s successor at Nvidia is gathering pace, marking a potentially significant leadership shift in the tech industry. After 33 years under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia is beginning the search for a permanent CEO. AMD’s Lisa Su, Arm’s Rene Haas and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress are among the names emerging in succession discussions. US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has floated an unexpected candidate: Apple’s Tim Cook. 

From leadership changes in global tech to regulatory developments closer home, Paytm has received an in-principle nod from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to revive its wallet business through a new subsidiary. The approval marks an important step in the fintech major’s efforts to rebuild its payments business, though it still needs final authorisation to resume operations.

Meanwhile, as satellite communications gain strategic importance, Bharti Enterprises Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal has cautioned India against relying on a single company for critical satellite infrastructure. He believes the country must retain control of the satellite communications 'kill switch' to safeguard national security and strategic autonomy.

In other news, Razorpay and Sembcorp Green Infra have received SEBI’s observations on their IPO papers, bringing them a step closer to the public markets. While Razorpay is reportedly eyeing a $500–600 million issue, Sembcorp Green Infra plans to raise Rs 3,750 crore.  

In the crypto world, the US Department of Justice has secured court approval to seize or restrain over $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance in a $6.3 billion hack attributed to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor. The move adds to more than $2.7 billion in funds frozen by US authorities and private-sector partners as efforts to recover the stolen assets continue. 

In today’s newsletter:  

  • One outage, millions affected. What went wrong at Microsoft? 
  • We have to stop linking child sexual abuse to family honour: Vidya Balan  

Here’s your trivia for today: Which country introduced the world's first public 5G mobile network? (Scroll down for the answer)

Explainers

One outage, millions affected. What went wrong at Microsoft? 

A disruption in Microsoft’s Exchange Online service triggered a global outage on November 12, affecting millions of users and businesses that rely on Microsoft 365. The disruption spread to Outlook, Copilot, Teams calendars and several connected workplace tools, with its impact extending to companies and government institutions worldwide. We break down what went wrong, why the outage affected so many services, and what it reveals about the risks of depending on shared cloud infrastructure. 

Key takeaways: 

  • Several servers unexpectedly became unavailable, overloading the remaining infrastructure. A process responsible for establishing secure connections was overwhelmed, while Microsoft also rolled back a recent network configuration change.
  • The disruption affected Microsoft 365 services, including Copilot, Teams calendars, Planner and Power BI. Businesses such as IndiGo and Akasa Air also reported issues with their email-support services.
  • When multiple workplace tools rely on the same underlying infrastructure, a single failure can disrupt entire business operations. Companies need backup communication channels and alternative ways to access critical information.

Social Impact

We have to stop linking child sexual abuse to family honour: Vidya Balan

Actor Vidya Balan is using her voice to challenge the silence and stigma surrounding child sexual abuse in India. As Goodwill Ambassador for NGO ARPAN, she is leading its eighth Child Safety Week campaign, #RukJaoVarnaPOCSOPakadLega, to raise awareness about abuse and the legal consequences for perpetrators. In a conversation with SocialStory, she discusses why family honour must never come before a child's safety, the importance of breaking the silence, and the role adults must play in protecting children. 

Key takeaways: 

  • Child sexual abuse must not be linked to family honour. Such stigma often results in victims being blamed and families choosing silence over accountability. 
  • Abuse goes beyond physical assault. Inappropriate touching, sexual remarks, gestures and online exploitation are also offences under the POCSO Act. 
  • Parents and teachers must build trust, educate children about personal safety, recognise grooming and respond with belief and support when a child speaks up.

News & updates

  • Energy Markets: The global oil market is set to return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026 for the first time since the Iran war began, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). Recovering Gulf exports are outpacing demand, with supply expected to exceed consumption by 1.7 million barrels per day, although continued attacks on shipping and infrastructure remain a risk to the recovery.

  • Space Tech: SpaceX is gearing up for the 15th test flight of its Starship rocket, with an ambitious plan to attempt the first land-based recovery of its upper-stage spacecraft at its Starbase facility in Texas. The mission will also attempt to bring back the Super Heavy booster using the launch tower’s mechanical arms, marking a major step towards developing a fully reusable rocket system. 

Which country introduced the world's first public 5G mobile network?

Answer: South Korea
